decision: Do not adopt the inlining hint as a fix for the frozen legacy encoding regression. Production serializer and fixture unchanged; no performance exception accepted.
experiment: Same isolated checkout and target directory; add only #[inline] to macro-generated CanonicalWireBytes methods. Normal frozen/opaque binaries captured before and after, then diagnostic-only explicit .text placement grid.
assessment: Normal frozen loop medians are 366.02 versus 361.22 ns/op; median paired change is -0.60%, with exploratory interval crossing zero. This does not establish a meaningful elapsed-time improvement.

Varied opaque input/output medians are 371.61 versus 335.84 ns/op; paired change is -10.82%. Whole-process instruction medians fall from about 861.08M to 813.59M, so this is not merely elimination of unobserved constant output.
Frozen default whole-process instruction medians also fall from about 854.80M to 805.03M. Instruction count and elapsed time are separate observations.

Each four-position grid keeps identical .text bytes within its source/fixture variant. The hint has mixed frozen timing effects: inline is slower at three of four matched placements and faster at one. It helps all four opaque matched placements in these runs.
Default .text changes from 279510 to 279542 bytes for the frozen fixture, and from 288230 to 284182 bytes for the opaque fixture. No general application binary-size or stack-size claim.

The smaller opaque profile demonstrates a possible optimization, but it does not close the retained frozen-workload flag. Stabilization keeps the existing serializer rather than adding a hint that lacks a reliable improvement on that gate.
limitations: Measurements are medians of process-loop averages, not individual-call p50/p95/p99 distributions. No allocations or stack measurements.

Opaque profile cycles four admitted DTOs including large sequence values, black-boxes input and entire output, compares complete bytes with serde_json::to_vec before timing, and checks aggregate byte count. Its absolute times are not interchangeable with the frozen fixture.
Counters cover each entire process, including bounded outcome-log append. They do not isolate the encoding loop.

Single host, Rust 1.100, CPU4, build CPUs4-7; fuzz rehearsal root observed after the diagnostic on CPUs8-15, no continuous descendant sampling or global cold-cache/host-load control. Rotated order and small diagnostic sample counts do not prove cross-platform equivalence.
Placement flags and extra benchmark stay isolated. No production linker setting, capacity, serializer, dependency or benchmark change is retained.
Initial driver aborted before building because of an invalid abbreviated reference; the corrected run pins the authoritative full baseline SHA. Failed initialization log/script retained.
Original legacy encoding and timeline findings, and exact final-source release qualification, remain open.
